Moral Foundations Theory is a framework that separates human morality into the following categories:

  - Care/Harm: related to our long evolution as mammals with attachment systems
    and an ability to feel (and dislike) the pain of others. It underlies the
    virtues of kindness, gentleness, and nurturance.

  - Loyalty/Betrayal: related to our long history as tribal creatures able to
    form shifting coalitions. It is active anytime people feel that it is "one
    for all and all for one." It underlies the virtues of patriotism and
    self-sacrifice for the group.

  - Authority/Subversion: shaped by our long primate history of hierarchical
    social interactions. It underlies virtues of leadership and followership,
    including deference to prestigious authority figures and respect for
    traditions.

  - Sanctity/Purity: shaped by the psychology of disgust and contamination. It
    underlies notions of striving to live in an elevated, less carnal, more
    noble, and more "natural" way (often present in religious narratives). This
    foundation underlies the widespread idea that the body is a temple that can
    be desecrated by immoral activities and contaminants (an idea not unique to
    religious traditions). It underlies the virtues of self-discipline,
    self-improvement, naturalness, and spirituality.

  - Equality: related to our intuitions about equal treatment and equal outcome
    for individuals.

  - Proportionality: related to our intuitions about individuals getting
    rewarded in proportion to their merit or contribution.

# Conservative Party Manifesto 2024: Summary

## Economic Policy

The manifesto outlines plans to reduce employee National Insurance from 12% to 6% by April 2027, representing a £1,350 annual reduction for average earners. Self-employed individuals would see their main National Insurance rate abolished entirely. The party commits to maintaining fiscal rules requiring public sector net debt to fall and borrowing to remain below 3% of GDP.

Business support includes maintaining corporation tax rates, extending "full expensing" to leasing when conditions allow, and a ten-point plan for SMEs covering business rates relief, VAT threshold reviews, and improved access to finance.

## Taxation and Pensions

The "Triple Lock Plus" would ensure State Pensions rise annually by the highest of inflation, earnings, or 2.5%, while introducing a new age-related personal allowance to prevent pensioners being drawn into income tax. Child Benefit reforms would move to a household-based system, with withdrawal beginning at £120,000 combined income.

## Immigration

Proposals include a legally binding annual cap on migration covering work and family visas, with Parliament voting on levels each year. The Rwanda removal scheme would continue, alongside reforms to asylum rules and increased visa fees. Health checks for migrants would be introduced, with potential Immigration Health Surcharge increases.

## Defence and Security

Defence spending would increase to 2.5% of GDP by 2030, with £10 billion invested in munitions production. Plans include continued Ukraine support, nuclear deterrent modernisation, and a National Defence and Resilience Plan.

## Healthcare

NHS spending would increase above inflation annually, with commitments to recruit 92,000 additional nurses and 28,000 doctors. Pharmacy First expansion, 250 new or modernised GP surgeries, and 50 Community Diagnostic Centres are planned. Social care cost caps would be implemented from October 2025.

## Housing

The target is 1.6 million new homes, achieved through brownfield development fast-tracking, planning reforms, and abolishing EU nutrient neutrality rules. First-time buyers would benefit from permanent Stamp Duty relief up to £425,000 and a new Help to Buy scheme.

## Education and Skills

Proposals include mandatory National Service for 18-year-olds (military or civic), 100,000 new apprenticeships funded by closing underperforming university courses, and the Advanced British Standard for 16-19 education. Mobile phones would be banned during school hours.

## Energy and Environment

Annual oil and gas licensing rounds would continue, alongside trebling offshore wind capacity and building Small Modular Reactors. Green levies on household bills would be kept lower than 2023 levels. Net zero by 2050 remains the target.

## Transport

£36 billion from HS2 savings would fund regional transport improvements, including £8.3 billion for road maintenance. The £2 bus fare cap would continue throughout the Parliament. Measures would prevent road pricing and reverse London's ULEZ expansion.

## Welfare Reform

Plans include reforming disability benefits assessment, tightening work capability assessments, and introducing stricter sanctions for those refusing suitable employment after 12 months. Projected savings total £12 billion annually.

# Green Party 2024 Manifesto Summary

## Overview

The Green Party's 2024 manifesto addresses the cost of living crisis, climate emergency, and public service decline. It proposes significant public investment funded through wealth taxation and borrowing.

## Health and Social Care

The manifesto proposes £28bn additional annual NHS spending by 2030, plus £20bn capital investment over five years. Key commitments include reducing waiting lists, guaranteeing GP access, ensuring NHS dentist availability for all, boosting staff pay, and restoring public health budgets. The party opposes NHS privatisation and supports the NHS Reinstatement Bill.

For social care, the manifesto proposes £20bn annual investment, free personal care, improved pay and career structures for carers, and increased disability benefits by 5%.

## Housing

The manifesto targets 150,000 new social homes annually, ending right-to-buy, empowering local authorities to introduce rent controls, and ending no-fault evictions. A £29bn five-year programme would retrofit homes for energy efficiency, with additional funding for heating systems and climate adaptation.

## Energy and Environment

The party proposes wind providing 70% of UK electricity by 2030, no new oil and gas licences, ending fossil fuel subsidies, and community ownership of energy sources. Nuclear power development would cease. A carbon tax starting at £120 per tonne would rise to £500 within ten years.

Environmental commitments include a Rights of Nature Act, 30% of land and seas protected by 2030, water companies returned to public ownership, and £1.5bn additional DEFRA funding.

## Economy and Work

The manifesto proposes £40bn average annual green investment, bringing railways, water companies, and major energy retailers into public ownership. A £15 minimum wage for all ages, maximum 10:1 pay ratios, and restored trade union rights are proposed. Anti-union legislation since 1979 would be repealed.

## Welfare and Cost of Living

Proposals include increasing Universal Credit by £40 weekly, ending the five-week benefit wait, abolishing the two-child cap, increasing carer's allowance by 10%, and scrapping the bedroom tax.

## Education

The manifesto proposes £8bn school investment including teacher pay increases, £2.5bn annually for building repairs, £5bn for special needs provision, free school meals for all children, scrapping tuition fees, and restoring maintenance grants.

## Transport

Proposals include £10bn annual public transport subsidies, railways returned to public ownership, free bus travel for under-18s, £2.5bn annually for cycleways and footpaths, ending new petrol and diesel vehicle sales by 2027, and opposing new road building.

## Democracy and Rights

The manifesto proposes replacing first-past-the-post with proportional representation, votes at 16, replacing the House of Lords with an elected chamber, defending the Human Rights Act, and repealing recent protest restriction legislation.

## Immigration

Proposals include ending the hostile environment policy, removing minimum income requirements for spousal visas, establishing safe asylum routes, permitting asylum seekers to work during applications, and ending immigration detention except for public safety cases.

## International Affairs

The manifesto calls for an immediate bilateral ceasefire in Gaza, recognition of Palestine, ending UK arms exports to Israel, restoring overseas aid to 0.7% of GNI rising to 1%, and rejoining the EU. On defence, it proposes signing the UN Treaty on the Prohibition of Nuclear Weapons and cancelling Trident, while remaining in NATO with reforms.

## Funding

Revenue would come from wealth taxes on assets above £10m, aligning capital gains and investment income tax rates with employment income, and carbon taxation. The party estimates raising £50-70bn annually from personal taxation reforms and up to £80bn from carbon taxes by parliament's end. Significant borrowing for investment is proposed, with inflation as the primary fiscal constraint rather than conventional debt rules.
